# network-xray

> Browser view of why a router chose its path, read from the live state of FRR / Nokia SR Linux / Cisco IOS-XE (IOL) routers in a containerlab or netlab lab. It shows the BGP candidate routes and the reason the best path won (Best-Path Decision), OSPF adjacency state and OSPF-learned routes, interfaces and the routing table, as a topology view plus a per-router "DeepDive". Read-only: it runs show commands and changes nothing.

## What it is
- A descriptive renderer of live router state, not a simulator and not a config checker.
- Input: live state, read-only commands only. FRR: `docker exec <node> vtysh -c '<show command>'`. SR Linux: `docker exec <node> sr_cli 'info from state … | as json'`. Cisco IOL: SSH, `terminal length 0` and `terminal width 0` (for that session only), then plain-text `show ip ospf neighbor`, `show ip ospf interface [brief]`, `show ip interface brief`, `show ip route`, `show ip bgp summary`, `show ip bgp`, `show ip protocols`, `show bridge-domain` (login `NX_IOS_USER` / `NX_IOS_PASSWORD`, default admin / admin).
- Output: a web page (topology + per-router DeepDive) that updates every few seconds while the lab runs.

## Supported
- Routers read (by containerlab kind, see `VENDORS` in clab-xray-collect.js): FRRouting (FRR); Nokia SR Linux (`nokia_srlinux`, clab-srl-collect.js); Cisco IOS-XE IOL (`cisco_iol`, clab-iosxe-collect.js; OSPFv2 and BGP, global table only). Other nodes (Linux hosts, cEOS, …) are drawn in the topology but not read.
- Lab tools: containerlab; netlab (as a netlab tool, netlab 26.10).
- Protocols shown: BGP (sessions, BGP table, best path and why), OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 (neighbors, interfaces and their areas, OSPF-learned routes; the LSDB panel lists the routes learned through OSPF, from the routing table (`show ip route … json` / `show ipv6 route … json`) — `show ip ospf database` is not read; SR Linux is the exception: its LSDB panel is read from its OSPF link-state database), static routes. OSPFv3 and VRFs: FRR only. Interfaces, routes, OSPF, BGP sessions and the BGP table (best path) inside VRFs are read too; on a router with VRFs the Routing table and the BGP Table show one VRF at a time (a VRF button switches; the management VRF `mgmt` gets no button). The IPv6 BGP table is not read. A passive OSPF interface is shown as a state, not as a fault.
- Image: ghcr.io/rclab-dev/network-xray:1 (linux/amd64, linux/arm64). License: MIT.

## FRR fields it reads
- `show ip bgp vrf all json`: per path `bestpath` (true for the winner) and `selectionReason` (FRR's reason), plus `locPrf`, `weight`, `path` (AS path), `origin`, `metric`, next hop. The Best-Path Decision panel compares the candidates on these fields.
- `show ip bgp vrf all summary json`, `show ip ospf vrf all neighbor json`, `show ip ospf vrf all interface json`, `show ip route vrf all json`, `show interface json`, `show running-config`. An FRR that does not answer a `vrf all` command in JSON (e.g. FRR 8.4 for routes) is read with the plain command (default VRF only).
- OSPFv3, only on routers with `router ospf6`: `show ipv6 ospf6 vrf all neighbor json`, `show ipv6 ospf6 vrf all interface json`, `show ipv6 route vrf all json`.
- netlab `validate:` tests (bgp_neighbor, bgp_prefix) are judged like `netlab validate`: per-prefix `show bgp ipv4 unicast <prefix> json`, winner = `bestpath.overall`.

## Start
- No install (recorded demo): https://rclab-dev.github.io/network-xray/demo/index-bgp-lp.html
- GitHub Codespaces (real 3-router FRR lab, needs a GitHub login): https://codespaces.new/rclab-dev/network-xray?quickstart=1
- containerlab: `git clone https://github.com/rclab-dev/network-xray.git && cd network-xray && ./xray.sh examples/q21-bgp-lp/q21.clab.yml` (deploys the lab; needs containerlab and Node.js; usage `./xray.sh [lab.clab.yml] [port] [template.html]`, port default 8080) then open http://localhost:8080/ (from another machine: http://<host-ip>:8080/)
- Any running containerlab lab: `docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -v "$(pwd)":/lab:ro -p 127.0.0.1:8600:8600 ghcr.io/rclab-dev/network-xray:1 --topo /lab/<lab>.clab.yml` then open http://localhost:8600/ (run it from the lab folder; `-p 8600:8600` opens it to other machines; options after `--topo`: `--port`, `--proto auto|ospf|bgp|static`, `--interval <s>`)
- netlab: add `defaults.sources.extra: [ <network-xray>/docker/netlab-defaults.yml ]` and `tools: { network_xray: }` to the topology, then `netlab up`; open http://<host>:8600/

## Query from scripts and AI assistants (read-only, no router contacted)
- Input `<path>`: a `state_<node>.json` or a directory of them (e.g. `test/fixtures/iosxe-q15`), the `xray-states.js` written by clab-xray-collect.js, or a directory of saved FRR `show … json` files (`frr-collect.js --from-dir` layout, e.g. `fixtures/frr-collect-sample/r1`).
- CLI: `node scripts/xray-query.js state <path>` (nodes, links, OSPF adjacencies, BGP sessions, counts) and `node scripts/xray-query.js why <path> <node> <prefix> [vrf]` (BGP best path and the stored reason; `reason` is null with a `note` when the data has none). Prints one JSON object (`--format table` for a plain-text table); errors print `{"error": "..."}` and exit 2.
- MCP server: `node scripts/xray-mcp.js` (stdio, JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line; MCP revisions 2024-11-05 to 2025-11-25). Tools: `lab_state {path}`, `why_best_path {path, node, prefix, vrf?}`, `list_routers {path}`, `ospf_neighbors {path, router?}`, `bgp_neighbors {path, router?}` `route_lookup {path, router, destination, vrf?}` and `why_path {path, router, prefix, vrf?}` (selected BGP path, other candidates, deciding step) (longest match in the collected routing table; it does not compute routing), read from the same state as xray-query.js. It only reads the given path: no commands, no file writes, no network. Claude Code: `claude mcp add network-xray -- node /path/to/network-xray/scripts/xray-mcp.js`.

## Tests (Node 18+, no dependencies, no package.json; run from the repo root)
- `node --test` runs `test/*.test.js` (fixtures in `test/fixtures/`).
- Self-tests: `node bgp-parse.js`, `node clab-collect.js --self-test`, `node clab-srl-collect.js --self-test`, `node clab-iosxe-collect.js --self-test`, `node frr-collect.js --self-test`, `node scripts/hello-kf-selftest.js`.

## Limits and cautions
- The container is given the Docker socket (root-equivalent on the host): use it on lab machines only.
- The page has no login and listens on all interfaces: keep it on a trusted network.
- With netlab, `network-xray.json` in the lab folder holds the lab's values (passwords included) while the lab is up; `netlab down` removes it.
- Not for production monitoring. For checking configs before deployment, use Batfish. For collecting and querying state across many devices over time, use SuzieQ.
- Single maintainer; pull requests are not accepted (forks are welcome).
